text:
Jonas Brodin has played 934 NHL games, all for Minnesota, and he's playing 22 and a half minutes a night for the best team in the West by record, at 12-3-4. He has no goals and seven assists in 19 games, six of them in his last ten.

He's a defensive defenseman, and the numbers fit. Evolving-Hockey had him 17th among 215 defensemen in wins above replacement last season, with opponents getting fewer chances against him than almost anyone (99th percentile). The Wild have 53% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice this season, and they've scored 4.9 fewer goals than those chances deserve, which has cost him points.

The weakness, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking: only 28% of his exits keep possession, so he clears the puck more than he carries it out. He's 33, the 10th pick in 2011, and his ice time is up over a minute lately. Our projection sees about 30 points.
